candidates.evidence_text: Greenfield homes were evacuated as fire raged at industrial site - BBC News Image caption, Homes in two streets were evacuated as flames engulfed an industrial unit By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 16 August 2026 Families had to be evacuated from their homes in two streets after a huge fire broke out at a neighbouring industrial building. The blaze, which shot huge plumes of black and orange smoke into the sky, was spotted at just after 07:30 BST at a site off Wellington Road in Greenfield, near Oldham. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said 45 homes were evacuated in Wellington Road and Knoll Close, which backs on to the burning building. Residents have now returned to their homes, with fire crews using gas detectors to ensure it was safe to do so, a spokesperson said. Image caption, The site backs on to houses on Knoll Close More than 10 fire engines along with a number of aerial ladder units and specialist appliances from across Greater Manchester were sent to the scene of the blaze. "Our crews remain at the scene, continuing their work alongside partners to make the site safe," the fire service added. A cordon was put in place during the incident and nearby roads were shut while crews tackled the fire. People were asked to avoid the area. candidates.lead: Bader Al-Akkad's "long journey" took in the war in Syria and a career-ending cancer diagnosis
candidates.evidence_text: A former footballer whose playing career was cut short by cancer has said co-founding a club in Dubai aimed at "giving people second chances" felt like "a massive achievement" Bader Al-Akkad, from Manchester, had to leave Stockport County's academy side after being diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma in 2021, ending his dreams of a professional contract After being given the all-clear, he started Phoenix United with his brother Amer, 27, to provide both sporting and academic opportunities to those wanting to follow their own footballing dreams "It's been a long journey of building... and to take this step now has been a massive achievement for us," said Bader, who is preparing for the side's first season in the UAE Third Division Bader and Amer were born in Manchester to Syrian parents, but spent their early years in Damascus after his family returned there They left Syria for the UK in 2012, a year after anti-government protests and a violent crackdown had escalated into conflict

candidates.evidence_text: Sixteen-year-old James Conway was working as a milkman when World War Two broke out in the September of 1939 Conway, from Edgeley in Stockport, signed up to join the Royal Marines where he trained for a secret mission, later named Operation Frankton He was among 12 men chosen to be part of what was widely considered to be one of the most audacious raids during the war Conway's story has featured in BBC Radio Manchester's Hidden Manchester series, which shares the forgotten, untold and heroic stories of the region By March 1942, Britain was struggling to fight back against Nazi Germany The mission was to attack enemy German ships, known as blockade runners, moored at the port of Bordeaux in occupied France

candidates.evidence_text: Fire chiefs in Greater Manchester have said the service is experiencing its busiest period in decades - as a series of serious blazes broke out at the peak of the recent UK heatwave Crews were already dealing with a large wildfire near Oldham on Wednesday when a semi-detached house also went up in flames in south Manchester the next day A raft of fires across the country, including devastating blazes in the West Midlands, later prompted the government to issue a temporary ban on disposable barbecues Greater Manchester's Chief Fire Officer Dave Russel thanked crews for their work in an "exceptionally busy period" while his deputy Jim Willmott said firefighters had received 1,200 calls on Thursday Willmott told BBC Radio Manchester : "Yesterday I was in the fire control room for North West Fire Control - it really was the most incredibly busy period I have ever seen in my 26 years of service." Earlier in the month crews stood down from wildfires on two stretches of moorland near Dove Stone Reservoir and at Tintwistle and Swineshore

candidates.title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit
candidates.summary: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
candidates.reason: Cheap pre-enrich duplicate remains suppressed after history checks.
candidates.practical_angle: Полиция или суд сообщили новое развитие по делу.
candidates.lead: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
candidates.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away The suspect was arrested at the scene of the crash on suspicion of theft of a motor vehicle, dangerous driving, failure to stop, driving under the influence of a controlled substance and possession of Class A and C drugs

Earlier in the month crews stood down from wildfires on two stretches of moorland near Dove Stone Reservoir and at Tintwistle and Swineshore

candidates.summary: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire

candidates.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-year-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 13:02, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Manchester The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:48, 16 Aug 2026 A family in Salford feel they are being ‘forced out’ of their home due to relentless abuse from a group of local teens - including eggs and rocks being thrown at their house The attacks have been going on regularly for almost two years and often feature racist or islamophobic abuse, leading the family to believe the harassment is targeted “I don’t want to leave my home, it’s an amazing area,” said Aram, 35, whose name has been changed for peace of mind, “But I feel I’m being forced out by these people who just have no shame. It keeps happening again and again and again. That’s why I’m upset.” Aram and his wife, who are both Kurdish, fled from Syria more than a decade ago and work as a pharmacist and doctor in the Salford area. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton 'Don't go up there': Weird moorland sacrifices, strange legends, and the fight to rebuild 'Two Lads' A mysterious presence on the West Pennine moors for centuries, the stone monuments, once believed to be the location of Druid sacrifices, are b News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17:30, 16 Aug 2026 Hundreds of people joined an archaeological dig days before stone cairns which date back to the Bronze age are rebuilt The ‘Two Lads’ stone monuments which have stood on the moors for time immemorial on Crooked Edge Hill, an outlying summit on Winter Hill, were dismantled in July and are now in the process of being rebuilt The iconic moorland stone landmarks high up on the West Pennine moors, north of Bolton , are on the Smithills estate managed by the Woodland Trust After a public consultation the trust is rebuilding the cairns into beehive shapes, with a new dry stone wall surrounding them It is hoped the restored monuments will continue to be a popular destination, with views of Bolton, the Manchester and Salford skyline, Liverpool docks, North Wales and even Barrow all being visible from the peak

There were various food stations, free hair cuts, clothes, drinks, an ice cream bar and a free chiropodist station Don’t Walk Past were told they would have to move their cars and vans by a parking warden but when they refused they received parking fines from Manchester Council. candidates.evidence_text: Strangeways Convicted killer found dead in Strangeways Lee Hopkinson had been jailed for 13 years for manslaughter View 3 Images Lee Hopkinson (Image: GMP) News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:32, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 07:26, 16 Aug 2026 A convicted killer found hanged in his cell in Strangeways left a note saying 'my head is gone and no-one can help me', an investigation into his death found Lee Hopkinson, who was jailed for the manslaughter of Raymond Dixon in Bury , took his own life in HMP Manchester in February 2022. The 33-year-old, who had a long history of drug problems and had previously been suspected of brewing 'hooch' in his cell, had drunk a 'significant' Hopkinson was jailed in 2019 for the manslaughter of Raymond Dixon in Bury. Mr Dixon, 50, was beaten to death by drug-addicted thug Edward Fitzgerald at his home in Myrtle Street North It came after Hopkinson spread a 'scurrilous rumour' about the 50-year-old being a paedophile then recruited Fitzgerald and Anthony Dennison to help him rob the 'vulnerable' and 'frail' man. After Fitzgerald attacked Mr Dixon, Hopkinson and Dennison searched his home for things t Manchester Crown Court heard that before his death Mr Dixon, who lived alone, had recently made friends with his next door neighbour. He told the neighbour about Hopkinson, who he said would regularly turn up at his home just before his benefits were paid

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham, where some are now ready to welcome 'the devil they don't know' One person said: “We have tried the devil we know. Maybe it’s the devil we don’t know that we need to go with.” View 6 Images Oldham is known for its divisive politics but News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:41, 16 Aug 2026 Some in Oldham are ready to welcome ‘the devil they don’t know’ after a months-long ‘Mexican stand off’ keeps going around in ‘vicious circles’ At the end of July, Oldham Council officially declared it is breaking the law with the cause of this being an ongoing row over who should be leading the local authority. After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. However if that were to happen, it would come at a cost of at least £1,200 a day

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-year-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 13:02, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Manchester The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

The aim is to minimise the impacts on residents as tens of thousands of people descend on the area for a weekend of music But figures released after this year’s event suggest that the scheme is not working. A Freedom of Information request reveals that 414 fines were issued for breaches for Parklife 2026 . 81 of these were later withdrawn Residents in the area said the event is ‘out of control’, with a number of people telling the Manchester Evening News that some event-goers are actively ignoring the parking restrictions because the cost of the fine – particularly when split between four or five passengers – is w Two residents living within the parking zone said they have previously stopped drivers to warn them about the restrictions, only to be told the charge each was low enough that it ‘doesn’t matter’. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

candidates.evidence_text: Traffic and travel Why are the M60 and M56 so bad? News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:48, 16 Aug 2026 A family in Salford feel they are being ‘forced out’ of their home due to relentless abuse from a group of local teens - including eggs and rocks being thrown at their house The attacks have been going on regularly for almost two years and often feature racist or islamophobic abuse, leading the family to believe the harassment is targeted “I don’t want to leave my home, it’s an amazing area,” said Aram, 35, whose name has been changed for peace of mind, “But I feel I’m being forced out by these people who just have no shame. It keeps happening again and again and again. That’s why I’m upset.” Aram and his wife, who are both Kurdish, fled from Syria more than a decade ago and work as a pharmacist and doctor in the Salford area. They originally lived in Fallowfield in Manchester, before they became eligible for a council house in a scheme through Salford Hospital for hi View 3 Images Egg thrown at the family's home

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton 'Don't go up there': Weird moorland sacrifices, strange legends, and the fight to rebuild 'Two Lads' A mysterious presence on the West Pennine moors for centuries, the stone monuments, once believed to be the location of Druid sacrifices, are b News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17:30, 16 Aug 2026 Hundreds of people joined an archaeological dig days before stone cairns which date back to the Bronze age are rebuilt The ‘Two Lads’ stone monuments which have stood on the moors for time immemorial on Crooked Edge Hill, an outlying summit on Winter Hill, were dismantled in July and are now in the process of being rebuilt The iconic moorland stone landmarks high up on the West Pennine moors, north of Bolton , are on the Smithills estate managed by the Woodland Trust After a public consultation the trust is rebuilding the cairns into beehive shapes, with a new dry stone wall surrounding them It is hoped the restored monuments will continue to be a popular destination, with views of Bolton, the Manchester and Salford skyline, Liverpool docks, North Wales and even Barrow all being visible from the peak

candidates.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-year-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 13:02, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Manchester The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

candidates.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

On the back of that, I’m afraid you’re just going to have to go further and do more,” he said

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.evidence_text: Thursday 23 July 2026 at 4:58pm King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court. Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

The annual budget increased from £2.4m to £5.5m to ensure essential A significant number of applications were received for the 2026–29 round and funding has now been allocated to 80 selected organisations Manchester is home to over 3,800 voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise organisations. Significant work has ensured this funding reaches communities who need it the most such as deprived wards, marginalised communities like disabled people and racially minoritised grou CEO Leah Chikamba-Mulando said she began the Angels of Hope for Women in 2014 because of the number of Black African women she was encountering who lacked confidence to access mainstream services in the UK Based in Gorton, the organisation became an officially registered charity in 2019, supporting women with anything from housing and immigration to benefits and domestic violence cases

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester saw more homes built in the last year (4,766) than all the 32 Greater London boroughs combined (4,261) a report to the Council’s Communities and Equalities Scrutiny Committee heard today (Weds 22 July) The significant achievement marks another record-breaking year as part of the Council’s ambitious housing strategy up to 2032, which also saw more affordable homes built than at any point since the late 1990s with 901 affordable tenure homes completed – of which around half (439) Manchester is also bucking the national trend for affordable housing starts recording an increase of 12% since 2022/23 And the city centre also saw the largest ever delivery of affordable in the city’s history over the last year with 259 completions, helping to diversify the city centre housing market and help more Manchester people have more choice about where they live The Housing Strategy update shows that the city remains on track to meet its target to deliver at least 36,000 homes of all tenures by 2032, including 10,000 social, Council and genuinely affordable homes – 3,000 of which will be in the city centre 13,555 homes have already been delivered since 2022 with more than 7,800 currently under construction, and a further 20,000 homes with planning approval or in the pipeline

candidates.lead: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
candidates.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8% The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton’s Best Start Family Hubs has achieved UNICEF’s stage 1 Baby Friendly Initiative status, recognizing the quality support it provides for parents and babies to protect them throughout life Bolton’s hubs, delivered in partnership with Bolton Council, Bolton NHS Foundation Trust, Bolton Together, Bolton CVS and GMMH NHS Foundation Trust, have been awarded the Baby Friendly Initiative by the UK Committee for UNICEF The award embraces the positive work culture, and staff knowledge, skills, and care provided to support parents, and it is the first step in assessments over several years that can lead to the highest Gold Award The UNICEF award establishes high standards globally in maternity, neonatal, and community health services to benefit babies, mothers, and families Encouraging more mothers to breastfeed is the main aim of UICEF as it supports parents to form close bonds with their children and also provides many other health benefits for both babies and mothers In particular, breastfeeding provides greater protection against infections, asthma, diabetes, and sudden infant death syndrome for the infant, and reduces the risk of cancer and heart disease for mothers

This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

The coffee shop has opened its doors to a series of culinary talents from across the city to take-over and host their own Late over the next few months. candidates.evidence_text: A thousand free pizzas will be up for grabs to celebrate one of Greater Manchester’s newest restaurant openings this week That’s right – award-winning Neapolitan pizzeria Forbici is officially opening at the Trafford Centre From 11am until 12:30pm this Wednesday (5 August), Forbici will be giving away up to 1,000 full-sized pizzas, so visitors to the shopping centre will have the chance to taste what has recently been declared one of the best pizzas in the world without needing to spend a penny Following the opening of its first site on Cross Street in the city centre last year, before expanding over to Sheffield, this new 7,000-capacity Trafford Centre space at The Orient will be Forbici’s third restaurant in the UK and the second in Greater Manchester Crafted with signature three-generation ‘biga dough’, slow fermented to create a light, airy crust, alongside carefully sourced Italian ingredients, it’s no secret that Forbici offers some of the finest pizza in town And staying true to its name, every pizza is cut with scissors before being served

candidates.evidence_text: A new food and drink concept is opening its doors in Altrincham today, serving perfect personal-sized pizzas by night, and coffee and croissants by day The much-loved Irish Deli has sadly closed its doors, but the team are immediately rolling in a brand-new concept for the town Under one roof, Paddy’s will be the new home of Flakey (famed for their enormous, filled sweet and savoury croissants) as well as a pizza and cocktail bar The two concepts will share the cosy space beside Kennedy’s Irish Bar, right in the heart of Altrincham Customers will be able to pop in Monday to Sunday to pick up Flakey’s stuffed croissants, along with speciality coffee and matcha There’ll be savoury fillings like the Buff Italian (vegetable caponata, buffalo mozzarella, and pesto) and the New Yorker (Emmental, pastrami, sauerkraut and pickles), plus sweet options like the Sticky BC (vanilla Basque cheesecake and Biscoff)

candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. candidates.evidence_text: Cyber start-up raises $7 million to tackle AI risk | Bdaily Ben Armstrong, left, and Thomas Ballin, founders of Cytix Cyber start-up raises $7 million to tackle AI risk A Manchester-based cybersecurity start-up has secured $7 million to accelerate the rollout of technology designed to tackle emerging risks created by rapid software development. Cytix has completed a Series A funding round led by Northern Gritstone, with participation from existing investors Auriga Cyber Ventures and NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance. The latter is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II. Bosses say the investment will support the rollout of Cytix’s newly launched change risk platform, which monitors software changes and updates to identify and validate potential security risks. They add the technology responds to growing pressure on organisations to keep security controls aligned with increasingly rapid software development, as AI-assisted coding, agentic workflows and continuous delivery accelerate the volume and pace of change. Ben Armstrong, chief executive of Cytix, said: “We chose Northern Gritstone for their conviction in investing in deeptech companies in the North of England with global ambition. “Northern Gritstone and Cytix share the belief that software change is becoming a key risk for organisations and those that build software need a solution that scales with the current pace of development. “We’re also grateful to the existing investors that have backed us since the early days and increased their commitment because they've seen the thesis play out.” Ben added: “Software is changing. “AI-assisted development means change now happens at machine speed. Meanwhile, very few security leaders have control over, or understanding of, those changes from a risk perspective. “Right now, existing tools can tell you what vulnerabilities you have, but can’t tell you about the risk. “We launched Cytix’ change risk management platform to get control of that risk.” Cytix’s platform, which entered general release yesterday (August 12), sits between a customer’s software development processes and its risk, security and compliance functions. It analyses what has changed, assesses the potential business risk, determines what security action is required and provides evidence showing how that risk was managed. The company says this can help organisations maintain oversight as increasing volumes of AI-generated code enter their systems. The funding will also help Cytix expand among enterprise and regulated businesses, where demonstrating effective governance of software changes can be a compliance requirement. Customers can access the technology directly through Cytix or via managed service partnerships with NCC Group and KPMG. Duncan Johnson, chief executive of Northern Gritstone, added: “The explosion of AI-assisted software development has led to a race to ensure software implementation remains secure. “Cytix’s platform aims to help enterprises take a realistic approach, recognising where change carries the most risk whilst allowing businesses to innovate. Northern Gritstone is proud to support another ambitious Manchester-based business in an exciting phase of its growth.” Sarah Isal, principal investor at Auriga Cyber Ventures, added: “We invested in Cytix because the team identified early that software change would become a critical cybersecurity challenge. “Since then, they’ve shown the resilience and discipline to execute on that vision, building a product that’s earning the trust of enterprise customers and strategic partners alike. “We’re proud to continue supporting Ben, Thomas and the team in this next phase of growth.” The £660 million NPIF II fund, which is operated by the British Business Bank, provides loans from £25,000 to £2 million and equity investment up to £5 million to help a range of small and medium sized businesses, driving innovation and creating opportunities for businesses to grow, scale, and thrive. Sue Barnard, senior investment manager at the British Business Bank, added: “Cytix is a great example of the ambitious technology businesses emerging from the North of England, developing innovative solutions to address the challenges created by the rapid growth of AI and software development. “Through the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II, we’re supporting businesses like Cytix that align with the Government’s Modern Industrial Strategy, helping to strengthen the North’s thriving

candidates.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

AMÒ is also an opportunity for Maurizio At the heart of the daytime offering is fresh pasta cooked daily by chef Valentina, with a £10 lunch deal on offer. candidates.evidence_text: From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ 11 April-11 July 2026 View dates and times Date Time Session Features 11 Apr 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm 11 Jul 2026 10:30 am-12:30 pm Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Is there any place in the UK that has changed so quickly and so utterly as Ancoats ? From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United Transfer News Man United told offer will be 'hard to reject' as manager speaks out on £30m target Manchester United are on the hunt for a new left-back this summer as they look to strengthen an area which will concern Michael Carrick Comments Spor Club Brugge manager Ivan Leko has admitted it will be "hard to reject" the right offer for Manchester United -linked Joaquin Seys. The Reds are looking to sign a new left-back this summer , with Luke Shaw having less than a year left on his current contract Patrick Dorgu, meanwhile, has looked more comfortable on the left wing, while two other options in that position, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazzrorui, are more right-backs. Harry Amass is another possibility for Michael Carrick , but is untested at the highest level Newcastle star Lewis Hall has been heavily linked with a summer switch to Old Trafford in United's search for left-back reinforcements. The 21-year-old is seen as the perfect age and already has good Premier League experience But a move to M16 is unlikely for now after the Magpies sold several key players this summer, including Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali. It means the Reds will have to explore other options with just over two weeks left before the transfer window slams shut FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! evidence_packet.lead: Monatik Europe Tour 2027. London at Indigo at The O2
evidence_packet.summary: Live-концерт MONATIK в Лондоне! 26 февраля 2027 года Indigo at The O2 превратится в место музыки, ритма и свободы, ведь на сцену выйдет вечно танцующий, невероятный исполнитель MONATIK!
evidence_packet.evidence_text: 26 февраля 2027 года Indigo at The O2 превратится в место музыки, ритма и свободы, ведь на сцену выйдет вечно танцующий, невероятный исполнитель MONATIK! Этот концерт — больше, чем просто выступление: это пространство, где публика сливается в едином ритме, проживая что-то настоящ MONATIK отправляется в международный концертный тур, в рамках которого посетит Великобританию! Артист влюбил миллионы слушателей в свою музыку благодаря песням “Кожний раз”, “А що?”, “Сильно”, “Кружить” и многим другим, в каждой из которых ритм занимает центральное место.
